name: ZEBRA Na|beta''-Al2O3|NaAlCl4|NiCl2 (tubular, 270-350 C)
salt_link: NaCl is the discharged cathode feed (cell assembled from NaCl + Ni powder); Na metal forms in situ on first charge
cathode: Ni/NaCl granules (+FeS, NaF, Al additives) in NaAlCl4 melt
E_source: OCV 2.58 V at 300 C [PUBLISHED, PS-008/PS-010]; 2.64 V from 298 K thermochemistry [CALCULATED, S11]
flammable: No organic solvent; molten Na is reactive (contained by ceramic + steel)
tox_note: Ni (sensitiser, Carc. 2 for powder), AlCl3/NaAlCl4 releases HCl with water
manuf_note: beta''-alumina ceramic + glass/TCB seals; few qualified suppliers
recyc_note: Ni/steel recovered in stainless-steel melt (historical practice)

name: IT planar Na|beta''-Al2O3|NaAlCl4|NiCl2 (190 C)
salt_link: Same as S01; planar format at 190 C (PNNL)
manuf_note: Planar ceramic discs + seals at lower T; pilot only

name: IT planar Na|beta''-Al2O3|NaAlCl4|FeCl2 (Fe + 10% Ni, 190 C)
salt_link: Assembled discharged from NaCl + Fe powder (+S additive) - salt and iron only for the active couple
E_source: OCV 2.35 V (Fe/FeCl2 vs Na, ~300 C) [PUBLISHED]; 2.41 V 298 K thermochemistry [CALCULATED, S11]
tox_note: Fe benign; AlCl3 hydrolysis to HCl remains

name: RT Na|AlCl3-SOCl2|Cl2-in-carbon (Na-Cl2)
salt_link: NaCl <-> Na + 1/2 Cl2 is the reaction itself; Cl2 stored in microporous carbon
rxn_cathode: 1/2 Cl2 + Na+ + e- -> NaCl (in carbon pores)
E_source: dG_f(NaCl) = -384.1 kJ/mol -> 3.98 V [CALCULATED]; cells run ~3.5 V [PUBLISHED PS-001]
flammable: Non-flammable solvent but SOCl2 is acutely toxic/corrosive; Cl2 gas on overcharge/abuse
tox_note: SOCl2 (fatal if inhaled, reacts with water -> SO2 + HCl); Cl2 gas
manuf_note: Li/SOCl2 primary-cell lines exist; rechargeable never manufactured
